expert_diagnosis: FTX suffered a catastrophic governance and liquidity failure rooted in the commingling of customer assets with affiliated-party (Alameda Research) operations, absence of meaningful segregation of customer funds, and a governance and control structure that was wholly inadequate for the scale of the exchange. When customer confidence collapsed and withdrawal demand surged, the exchange was unable to honor obligations, revealing a fundamental insolvency masked by governance opacity.
expert_first_action: Immediate controlled halt of new deposit acceptance and withdrawal processing pending independent verification of customer asset segregation, with simultaneous preparation for Chapter 11 filing if customer asset shortfall is confirmed.
actual_decision: FTX Trading Ltd. and affiliates filed voluntary petitions for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on 11 and 14 November 2022. John J. Ray III was appointed CEO. First-day declaration described severe liquidity crisis requiring emergency Chapter 11.
harmful_actions: Commingling of customer funds with Alameda Research operations
Absence of customer asset segregation in exchange operations
Governance and control structure wholly inadequate for scale of exchange
Use of FTT token as collateral creating circular and fragile balance sheet
Abandonment of Binance rescue deal without alternative solution
Failure to disclose true financial position to customers and regulators
beneficial_actions: Chapter 11 filing provided formal framework for customer and creditor claims
Appointment of experienced restructuring CEO (John J. Ray III) enabled professional administration
Kroll appointment as claims and noticing agent provided structured claims process
citation: Kroll bankruptcy docket for FTX restructuring proceedings. PACER first-day declaration by John J. Ray III. Reuters reporting on FTX bankruptcy and $6 billion withdrawal crisis. Kroll PDF of first-day declaration.
actual_outcome: FTX Trading Ltd. and affiliates filed Chapter 11 on 11 and 14 November 2022. John J. Ray III appointed CEO and described severe liquidity crisis in first-day declaration. Criminal proceedings followed against FTX founders. Customer assets substantially impaired at time of filing. Estate recovery processes initiated through Kroll-administered claims process.
documented_root_causes: Liquidity crisis from customer-run exceeding available liquid assets
Customer fund trust failure through commingling with Alameda Research
Governance and control failure at fundamental level
Related-party exposure between FTX and Alameda Research
Balance-sheet opacity concealing true financial position
Rescue-deal dependency (Binance) that was abandoned leaving no alternative
final_business_state: Chapter 11 filed 11-14 November 2022. John J. Ray III appointed CEO. Criminal proceedings initiated against founders. Customer asset recovery process through bankruptcy estate. Exchange operations ceased.
